label: monk2-s4
summary: The network approximates "exactly two of a1, a2, a3, a4 and a6 take their first value" and largely ignores a5's first value, which the MONK-2 target also counts. A linear tally of direct edges raises the score with each first value; a two-unit counter over a1, a2, a3, a4 and a6 opens on the 112 training rows with three or more such first values (share 100%) and lowers the score by 103.2 on average there; a gate lifts the score when a5 is not at its first value, and the direct a5:1 edge pays most of that back. Over all 432 attribute combinations the model agrees with the five-attribute rule on 416 and with the six-attribute target rule on 380; training accuracy is 88.7%, and 38 of the 39 training errors have a5 = 1. Switching off the counter, the tally or the a5 gate lowers the training AUC from 0.925 to 0.454, 0.811 and 0.878. Coverage is full and the explained structure matches the network to 4.4e-16.

The penalty for a5 at its second or fourth value (switching it off moves the training AUC from 0.9254 to 0.9255) and the a1 = 2 offset (AUC 0.9254 without its variation) are level offsets with no role in the rule, and node 927 is dead (open on 0 of 345 training rows).
